description: B1'S GUARD AT A CORNER STAIR (DECK-GUARD-OPENING; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B1, IRC R312): B1 at loft.deck 1.3.0 with its guard on the open sides and every other default, and b1-stair-30's loft.stair 1.0.0 on the rim moved flush with the deck's left corner (centred at X 18, its outer stringer faces X 0 and X 36). The run of the front guard from the corner to the stair is 0 in, under the two posts' 7 in, so the guard ends on the corner post (the left side's, X 0..3.5, on the decking): it stays, and it is the opening's post on that side; the opening's other post stands on the right stringer's face, X 36..39.5. model.json is EXACTLY the two expansions with their member materials; members.json each body's metadata (packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_deck_guard_opening.py pins both; services/geometry/tests/test_deck_guard_opening_b1.py checks the STEP against an independent build123d script, the opening, interference and the cut list).
derivation: INDEPENDENT of the plugins: test_deck_guard_opening_b1.script('b1-stair-30-guard-corner') is test_stair_b1's B1 (71 735.979474 in^3) and its stair moved to X 18 (4 062.891133 in^3, b1-stair-30's by translation), and the guard typed from buildings.md B1 and IRC R312. The STEP matches the 156 solids solid for solid (volume to 1e-4 in^3, bounds to 1e-5 in).

the guard stands on the decking (Z 30..66). The left and right sides are whole, Y 0..144: posts at Y 1.75, 72, 142.25, two bays of 66.75 clear, 12 balusters a bay. The front is broken at X 0..36: the run to the corner is the corner post alone (X 0..3.5, the left side's end post); the run X 36..192 (156 in) has posts at both ends, 37.75 and 190.25, 152.5 / 72 -> 3 bays of 50.8333 on centres: X 36..39.5, 86.8333..90.3333, 137.6667..141.1667, 188.5..192, three bays of 47.3333 clear, ceil((47.3333 - 4) / 5.5) = 8 balusters each. Posts 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

rails, 2x4 on edge, Z 33.5..37 and 62.5..66: a course 133.5 + 3 x 47.3333 + 133.5 = 409 in (the front 192 - 36 - 4 x 3.5 = 142), 818 over both, against the closed guard's 890. Balusters 2x2, Z 37..62.5: 24 + 24 + 24 = 72.
surface_area, centroid, mass_g and center_of_mass are the script's solids summed (expected_numbers()): southern_pine_pt 582 and concrete 2400 kg/m^3.

topology: b1-stair-30's 378 faces, 768 edges and 61 shells plus 95 boxes (9 posts, 14 rails, 72 balusters) of 6 faces and 12 edges: 948, 1 908, 156. MESH counts are recorded, not derived: 3 036 + 95 x 24 = 5 316 vertices and 2 280 + 95 x 12 = 3 420 triangles, as measured.

Interference none (exact probes): the corner post stands on the decking (Z 30) over the stair's left stringer, which hangs under it (Z <= 29) from the rim's face at Y 144 (the post stops at Y 144); the stair's handrail posts (X -3.5..0) start at its top nosing, Y 146.125.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill), b1-stair-30-guard-opening's class: the kernel differs from the script by -6.2e-6 mm^3 on the volume (the summation's ULPs over 156 solids, 4e-15 relative), 1.5e-8 mm^2 on the area, <= 6.8e-12 mm on the centroid and centre of mass and 1.4e-9 g on the mass. 3e-5 is 4.8x the volume's; a baluster missed takes 9.4e5 mm^3 (57.375 in^3) and a post moved 1/16 in moves the centroid 7.9e-3 mm, so either fails by more than two orders.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: KERNEL-LEVEL, measured 2026-10-30, b1-stair-30's class: OCCT's STEP writer rounds the notched stringers' and the sloped handrail's irrational coordinates, and the 156 re-imported solids sum in another order. Round-trip drift: volume -1.4e-5 mm^3, area +6.7e-7 mm^2, centroid 1.0e-11 mm (plugin); the independent build123d twin (script(), exported with build123d's export_step) drifts -3.1e-5 / -9.5e-7, so it is OCCT's STEP, not Loft's export. 1e-4 is 3.2x the worst (the twin's); it applies to volume and area only, the centroid and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL.
